_about: Monier-Williams (1899) text abbreviations -> what the locus means, which edition MW cites (as far as it can be established), which open edition we relocate into and how. Expansions are the Cologne mwauth tooltip (csl-pywork, mw_src/mwauth_tooltip.txt). MW's own 'List of Works and Authors' (1899, pp. xxxiii-xxxvi) exists only as print: Cologne's preface transcription and scan series stop at p. xxxii and no machine-readable copy was found, so 'mw_edition' is taken from the shape of the loci and the standard identifications (Böhtlingk-Roth's conventions, which MW follows) and is marked 'inferred' where MW's list was not read. Counts are citations with a numeric locus from mw_citation_census.json; 'well_formed' = the expected number of numeric parts.

RV..mw_edition: the standard maṇḍala/hymn/verse numbering (Aufrecht / Müller), identical in every edition
RV..method: A: align DCS sentences to GRETIL verses (consonant skeleton), unit = verse

Mn..mw_edition: Loiseleur Deslongchamps (1830) / Jolly (1887) numbering (inferred); Kullūka numbering in GRETIL differs by a few verses in some chapters

AV..verse_source: GRETIL avs___u.htm (TITUS text, refs (AVŚ_1,14.2a); 'for reference purposes only', terms as TITUS)

BhP..mw_edition: Burnouf (Paris 1840-47) / Bombay ed. (inferred; one locus carries 'B')
BhP..dcs: Bhāgavatapurāṇa (117 chapters, 77,814 tokens; skandhas covered partly)

Kathās..mw_edition: Brockhaus (1839-66): taraṅga numbered through the work (inferred from the shape)
Kathās..dcs: Kathāsaritsāgara (65 chapters named lambaka, taraṅga-in-lambaka; 188,181 tokens)
Kathās..verse_source: GRETIL sa_somadeva-kathAsaritsAgara (refs sokss_1,1.1 = lambaka,taraṅga.verse; Durgāprasād ed.)
Kathās..method: A; continuous taraṅga -> lambaka,taraṅga by the standard lambaka sizes (8,6,6,3,3,8,9,7,6,10,1,36,3,2,5,8,2,8 taraṅgas)

Kum..verse_source: ambuda-org/dcs kumarasambhavam.txt (DCS export with ids Ku.1.1; CC BY 4.0) and GRETIL sa_kAlidAsa-kumArasaMbhava (Ks_1.1)
Kum..method: C: join DCS sentences to the ambuda export by lemma sequence; fallback A

Bhartṛ..locus: śataka (i nīti, ii śṛṅgāra, iii vairāgya), verse
Bhartṛ..mw_edition: Bohlen (1833) (inferred; numbering of the śatakas differs between editions)

Megh..method: C with the continuous number split at the pūrvamegha's length; flagged, low confidence

Hit..locus: book (i-iv), verse  (41 of 108 are page,line of an edition: out)

ŚBr..verse_source: Hellwig VPC corpus/VPC/Brahmana texts/ŚBM.txt (ids kāṇḍa.adhyāya.brāhmaṇa.kaṇḍikā.sentence; CC BY 4.0)
ŚBr..method: B: join DCS sentence to VPC line by identical text within the chapter, unit = kaṇḍikā

TS..dcs: Taittirīyasaṃhitā (217 chapters = kāṇḍa.prapāṭhaka.anuvāka; 47,990 tokens; prose parts only in VPC)
TS..verse_source: DCS chapter = MW's first three parts; the fourth (section) has no counterpart in the dump
TS..method: B': window = the cited anuvāka (chapter), flagged chapter-level

AitBr..locus: pañcikā, khaṇḍa, section (116) or pañcikā, khaṇḍa (175)

Kāṭh..mw_edition: Schroeder (1900-10) numbering as in MW's day (inferred)

TāṇḍyaBr..verse_source: DCS chapter; VPC PB.txt sentence ids

Lāṭy..method: B (DCS holds almost none of it: expect ~0)

Gaut..dcs: Gautamadharmasūtra (28 chapters named praśna.adhyāya: 1.1-1.9, 2.1-2.9, 3.1-3.10 = adhyāyas 1-28 in order; 5,709 tokens)
Gaut..verse_source: DCS chapter (adhyāya) + sentence order for the sūtra
Gaut..method: B': window = chapter, sūtra by sentence order if it fits

Pāṇ..dcs: Aṣṭādhyāyī (32 chapters = adhyāya.pāda, 15,455 tokens, 3,982 sentences = sūtras)
Pāṇ..method: A; reported as its own stratum: most Pāṇ. citations justify a formation and the headword is not a token of the sūtra (prediction: <= 10% located)

MBh..locus: parvan, verse numbered through the parvan
MBh..mw_edition: Calcutta ed. (1834-39), continuous verse count per parvan (Böhtlingk-Roth's convention; 4 loci say Bomb./Calc.)
MBh..why: no Calcutta -> critical-edition verse concordance in machine form (a 2026 paper reports ~88% verse alignment; not published as data). v0.1: build the concordance from the GRETIL critical text and the Calcutta scan, or by monotone alignment of adhyāya sizes

R..mw_edition: Bombay ed. (B.) and Gorresio's Bengal recension (G./Gorr.), unmarked = Bombay (inferred; 57 loci carry the mark)
R..why: Bombay/Gorresio sarga and verse numbers differ from the critical edition's throughout; a concordance exists in print (Baroda ed. appendices), not in data

Yājñ..why: no verse-numbered open text found at GRETIL; v0.1 candidate (sanskritdocuments.org text, licence to check)

VS..why: no verse-numbered open text at GRETIL (TITUS has one, restricted); v0.1 candidate

Nir..why: DCS holds a fragment; chapter scheme unclear

Suśr..locus: mostly volume, page, line of the Calcutta ed. (1835-36)
Suśr..why: page-and-line loci do not map to a text structure without the printed edition

Car..locus: sthāna, adhyāya (, section) of the Calcutta ed.
Car..why: most loci are two-level (sthāna, adhyāya) = a whole chapter of 1,000+ words; v0.1 with a chapter-level route

Śak..locus: page, line of MW's own edition (1876)

Divyāv..why: page/line; GRETIL's text carries Cowell-Neil page numbers (001.001) so a v0.1 page-level route is possible

Ragh..why: not in the DCS dump (GRETIL has it; needs a lemmatized text or the oracle alone: v0.1 with vidyut as the only oracle)

Pañcat..why: not in DCS (Tantrākhyāyikā is); MW cites Kosegarten's ed. by book and verse or page

VP..why: no verse-numbered open text checked yet; v0.1 candidate

Dhātup..why: a root list, not a text

Uṇ..why: grammatical sūtras; the headword is the derived form, not a token

L. / W. / MW. / Cat. / Kāv. / Pur. / Bud.why: no locus (lexicographers, Wilson, MW's first edition, catalogues, literary categories, ibidem)
